item.title: Snow leopard cub Sarka born at Bronx Zoo
item.description: A female snow leopard cub has been born at the Bronx Zoo in New York on May 31, as the daughter of parents Dariga and Moutig. The cub, named Sarka (Nepali for 'shark'), passed her medical examinations and vaccinations and is now exploring the Himalayan Highlands habitat of the zoo alongside her mother. The zoo currently houses eight snow leopards....

item.title: Music education linked to lower school absenteeism in Rhode Island
item.description: A new study by Quadrant Research, commissioned by the Rhode Island State Council on the Arts, shows that students who take music lessons for four years are chronically absent from school less often. Among four-year music students, 25.4% were chronically absent, compared to 37.3% of students without four consecutive years of music. For arts subjects in general, the difference was...

item.title: Horizon Europe receives €500 million extra for research and innovation
item.description: The European Commission has released an additional €500 million for Horizon Europe, the EU's research and innovation programme, for 2026 and 2027. This brings the budget for these two years to approximately €14.8 billion. The funding will go towards two new calls for proposals: €237 million for eleven projects on biodiversity and a nature-positive economy, and €260 million for sixteen...

item.title: Red-legged frog returns to Yosemite after 50-year absence
item.description: About fifty years ago, the red-legged frog disappeared from Yosemite National Park, due in part to habitat loss, invasive American bullfrogs, and an increase in raccoons. Park staff removed the bullfrogs and restored wetlands and riverbanks. In 2016, a breeding program began at the San Francisco Zoo, where frogs are raised from wild-collected eggs until they reach one to two...

item.title: The Bulwark raises over $400,000 for Haitians in Springfield
item.description: Media outlet The Bulwark held a live show in Springfield, Ohio on September 25, with all proceeds going to the Haitian Support Center. This nonprofit assists the Haitian community with food, transportation, legal aid and other basic needs amid large-scale ICE operations in the city. item.description: In Meru National Park in Kenya, rangers from the Kenya Wildlife Service heard trumpeting elephants near an old well in the morning. item.title: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library doubles reach in London
item.description: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which has been sending free books to children under five since 1995, is expanding in London. The programme is growing from five to ten of London's 32 boroughs, enabling 157,000 additional children to receive a free book each month. The expansion was announced less than a month after Parton's death this year. Jeff Conyers, president of...

item.title: Olive ridley sea turtles nest for first time on US West Coast
item.description: For the first time, olive ridley sea turtles have been spotted nesting on the American West Coast. A female laid eggs at Seal Beach, and three days later another did the same at Huntington Beach. Scientist Lindsey Peavey Reeves called it unexpected. NOAA and Fish and Wildlife Service installed nets and barriers for protection. Due to extreme tides and hurricanes...

item.title: Sandilands golf course becomes wetland for rare seabirds
item.description: On the English coast, National Trust golf course Sandilands in Lincolnshire, purchased in 2020, has been transformed into a wetland nature reserve the size of 45 football pitches. No pesticides or drinking water are applied to the site anymore. item.title: Chris Evans helps inseparable dogs Greg and Carley find new home
item.description: Actor Chris Evans stepped in for two inseparable dogs, chihuahua Greg and golden retriever Carley, who needed to be adopted together. They were staying at the Animal Rescue League of Boston. Evans participated in 'Dream Date', a series by The Dodo in which Hollywood stars spend time with dogs looking for new homes. item.title: Orphaned elephant Daba adopted by herd in Kenya
item.description: On September 30, 2025, rangers from the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust and the Kenya Wildlife Service found an 8-month-old elephant alone north of the Galana River. They suspect that lions had chased away her herd, the Dabaduki group. The calf was named Daba, which means 'abandoned'. After the Voi Reintegration Unit, she was brought to the Nairobi Nursery for specialized care....

item.title: Bull elephant 'adopts' orphan calf Talek until rescue came
item.description: In June 2023, a seven-month-old orphaned elephant calf was spotted at the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya. When rangers searched for her, she had disappeared. A few days later, she reappeared, this time following an older male elephant who offered her protection. item.title: 12-year-old Sloan collects 30,000 diapers for Arizona food bank
item.description: For the fifth year in a row, 12-year-old Sloan from Phoenix organized her 'Diaper Drive', a diaper collection initiative. This year she aimed for 22,500 diapers, but ultimately 30,000 units arrived — so many that there was barely room to walk around in her house. The diapers, including brands such as Huggies, Pampers and Bluey, were delivered by Uhaul truck...

item.description: Socktober began 15 years ago when high school students wanted to help after learning that many people in their community were homeless or shuttling between shelters. A call to the local shelter revealed that socks were desperately needed but rarely donated. Schools, churches and businesses participated, collecting more socks than could fit in a car. item.title: Tanzanian farmers return land to elephants
item.description: In the Kilombero Valley in Tanzania, 368 farmers have ceded land to provide elephants with safe passage between the Udzungwa Mountains and Nyerere National Park. After seven years of preparation by the Southern Tanzania Elephant Program (STEP) and partners, the Nyerere-Udzungwa Wildlife Corridor (NUWC) received official protection in April 2025, the first of its kind in Tanzania. item.title: Japan records 107,677 centenarians, surpassing 100,000 milestone
item.description: According to recently published figures from the Ministry of Health, Japan has 107,677 residents aged 100 or older, marking the first time the 100,000 threshold has been exceeded. This makes Japan home to the world's largest population of centenarians. When the count began in 1963, there were 153; the 1,000 mark was crossed in 1981, and 10,000 in 1998. Eighty-eight...

item.title: Students name 309-million-year-old Jeanerpeton mazonensis after their mothers
item.description: Student scientists Allison Sefcovic and Payton Kohlberg have named a newly identified early amphibian species after their mothers, both named Jean. Jeanerpeton mazonensis lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs, in the area around present-day Chicago, then a swampy river delta. The creature resembled a salamander but was stocky and pudgy like a frog. The fossil was found...

item.title: Norway protects Andfjorden: whales and coral safe
item.description: Norway established a new marine protected area on September 18: the Andfjorden Marine Protected Area, covering approximately 714 square miles (nearly 260,000 football fields). The area is located in northern Nordland and southern Troms, and encompasses waters near Andøy, Harstad and Senja. item.title: Paid photos turn Borneo hunters into orangutan protectors
item.description: On the Indonesian island of Borneo, in West Kalimantan province, residents of 9 villages can earn money by taking photos or recording sounds of wild animals.
